value.why: Tier W is the only GPU tier, but its admission test needs (iii) one bounded surface, never page-wide chrome, and it must never become a 3D engine (three.js is named as the thing it must not grow into). This scene is page-wide, a 3D mesh with refraction, and every route sits on it. Comes back as a Bean trim/exclude decision (W4-c termination rule).

value.effect: menu items drawn into per-item canvases (2D context) with a live dissolve: the hovered item goes to a near-constant high lit-pixel count while the other two lose 40 to 98 per cent of theirs
value.why: Tier V has a canvas 2D substrate (FR-38-32 particle trail and FR-38-33 grid-dot field use it), so a per-item 2D text dissolve is expressible as a new Tier V effect, but none exists. Rendering the label only into a canvas removes real text, which SGS must not do; the nearest built effect is FR-38-11 ScrambleText (Tier G, on real DOM text), which is a different look. So: no built tier effect matches; expressible in principle as a new Tier V effect that keeps the DOM text.

value.effect: hero title drawn partly in the DOM and partly elsewhere: innerText reads "Re n · Creative Studio / E t. 2004" (letters missing) while the rendered title shows every letter
value.why: Per-character treatment of real DOM text is Tier G SplitText / ScrambleText territory (FR-38-10, FR-38-11); drawing some glyphs outside the DOM, and the chromatic fringing around the title, are not expressible by any tier.
